title: GPT-6 Helps Disprove the 2004 Undirected Multiple-Unicast Network Coding Conjecture
whyItMatters: Refutes Li & Li’s 22-year-old Multiple-Unicast Conjecture—showing network coding strictly outperforms routing in undirected networks with an Ω((log n)^ε) gap via a GPT-6-found Reed–Solomon counterexample.
summary: Mark Braverman and Zhongtian He refuted the famous 2004 Undirected Multiple-Unicast Conjecture of Li and Li, which posited that network coding offers no throughput advantage over multicommodity routing for multiple-unicast sessions in undirected graphs. Using GPT-6 to discover a nondeterministic Reed–Solomon local-code construction on a 182-vertex subgraph of the projective plane PG(2,9), the authors converted it into a deterministic linear network code over 𝔽_9 achieving rate ≥ 1 for 157 sessions where maximum fractional multicommodity flow is 147/157, and lifted it via tensoring to an asymptotic Ω((log n)^ε) coding-over-routing gap.
technicalHighlights: Refutes Li & Li’s 2004 Multiple-Unicast Conjecture after 22 years, resolving one of the central open problems in network information theory.
GPT-6 discovered the underlying nondeterministic Reed–Solomon local-code counterexample on a 182-vertex subgraph of PG(2,9).
Yields a deterministic linear network code over 𝔽_9 supporting 157 unicast sessions at rate ≥ 1 vs. max fractional flow 147/157, amplifying to an Ω((log n)^ε) gap.
caveats: Currently an October 2026 arXiv preprint (arXiv:2610.10108) undergoing community verification and peer review; not yet formally verified in Lean.

scoreRationale.foundational: Settles one of the deepest 21st-century conjectures in network coding and communication complexity by proving a super-constant coding advantage.
scoreRationale.ripple: Impacts information theory, graph sparsifiers, multicommodity flow gaps, and algebraic coding theory.
scoreRationale.verification: Explicit finite 182-vertex algebraic counterexample authored by Fields-medal-caliber TCS researchers (Abacus Medal winner Braverman), awaiting formal journal review.
scoreRationale.velocity: GPT-6 surfaced the finite projective-plane Reed–Solomon counterexample that cracked a 22-year barrier.
